_comment: FACTORtv — THE FIRST-RUN INTRODUCTION, spoken by the race engineer.
Asked for: 'when someone first launches there can be voice tutorial on what
buttons do what, so like the first load they will get a caption card being
narrated by the enginner to show them exactly how to use it'.
AN ORDERED SCRIPT, NOT A POOL. Every other line in this product is one of
several ways to say a thing, chosen at random and varied on purpose. This is
the opposite: it is a sequence, it has to arrive in order, and a driver hears
it once. So it is a list rather than a bag, and nothing here rotates.
`point` names a thing on screen to mark while the line is spoken — the words
'top left' are worth much less than the button lighting up as he says them.
Only 'menu' and 'trophy' exist; anything else marks nothing, which is a
IT IS THE ENGINEER, and it stays in his register: what to do, in the fewest
words, with no sales pitch. He does not welcome anybody to an experience.
KEEP IT SHORT. Nine lines is already most of a minute of talking at a moment
when the player wants to go driving, and the one thing worse than no
introduction is one he sits through resenting.

steps.t: Right, before you go anywhere. I am your engineer, and I will be on this channel all weekend.
Top left is the menu. Everything the overlay draws is switched on and off in there.
Next to it, the trophy. That is your career: your championship, your results, and your post.
If you have not started a career, open the trophy and start one. Every race you run after that counts towards it.
The number on the trophy is unread post. Letters from the team, the governing body, and people who matter to you.
In the car you get the timing tower, the relative panel and your dash. Turn off what you do not want to look at.
There are commentators on the race and on qualifying, and they know your career. They do not talk over practice, so practice is you and me.
One last thing. If you want a race that does not count, switch the round off in the career screen first, and none of us will treat it as a championship round.
That is everything. Go and drive, and talk to me about the car.
